title: Nevada National Guard ready to fight wildfires from the ground and air
description: This video shows Nevada National Guard Soldiers training as Type 2 wildland firefighters alongside the Nevada Division of Forestry, highlighting ground operations, fire shelter deployment, and aerial firefighting capabilities supporting wildfire response in Washoe Valley, Nevada, Apr. 23, 2026.
keywords: Wildfire response, Washoe Valley, NVNG, Davis Fire, National Guard, Type 2 Wildland Firefighter

transcript.text: As wildfire season approaches , the
Nevada National Guard is ready to
respond from both the ground and the
air . In the past week , about 40
soldiers completed wildland
firefighting training with the Nevada
Division of Forestry , earning Type 2
certification . So the training we've
got going on today is we're going to
probably run through a scenario where
we've got to go ahead and dig some line
out and things like that just to go
ahead and make sure that we're thinking
on the spot to make the proper
considerations when attacking the fires .
They trained on fire lines , shelter
deployment , and how fire behavior and
weather impact operations . It's nice
knowing that they're eager to learn .
They want to . Learn this and having
them trained in the same way that we do
just makes our jobs that much better
when we're on the fire line . We can
then incorporate them into squads and
they're going to have the exact same
training . So when we implement them
with a task or a mission , they're
going to be able to accomplish it just
like we would . At the same time , Air
Guard crews completed MAFS
recertification training in California .
The C-130 aircraft can drop up to 3000
gallons of fire retardant in seconds to
support firefighters on the ground .
The Nevada Army Guards aviation units
add another layer of support using
Black Hawk and Chinook helicopters for
water bucket drops and aerial support .
That combined capability was used
during the 2024 Davis fire in Washoe
Valley . Guardsmen worked 14 to 16 hour
shifts alongside forestry crews ,
helping contain the fire . Some
guardsmen like Sergeant Skylar Lujan
were activated just Two weeks after
their training back in 2024 . So we got
out there first day and we defended
some of the homes down here on the
lower side of the mountain , and we're
just separating that fuel from the
houses so if the fire does come , the
chances of them burning are less likely .
Through training and partnerships with
local agencies , the Nevada National
Guard remains ready to protect
communities across the state . I'm not
only just working , but I'm working for
the community , so it's a win-win . You
can't lose there .
